name: Broadleaf Plantain

facts.how: Young leaves raw or cooked; seeds as a psyllium-like fiber
facts.value: Vitamins A, C, K; the seed is a fiber source

caution: A safe, mild, extremely common plant. Take young leaves, and harvest away from sprayed lawns. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A flat rosette of oval leaves with strong parallel veins that string like celery when you tear one, and a slim seed spike up the middle. Not the banana.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: The youngest leaves are a mild salad green; older ones cook down. The seed is the same family as store-bought psyllium fiber, and the crushed leaf is a famous field poultice for stings.
